signals.evidence: Braeam (Bareqem): Residents lack individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); continuous shelter stays due to absence of home protection. Farmers report limited armored field booths (מיגוניות) relative to land area. Request for regular food supply.
Community leaders reported distrust in politicians and military: 'They told an unrealistic story, promised a quiet and safe border—it did not happen.'
Braeam: Lack of protected spaces for educational and social activities; no suitable public space available.
Braeam: Informal activity began; request for HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) training and volunteer reinforcement; elderly receiving community support.
Goren/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Young people fled; those aged 40+ remained. Narrative to stay accompanied by difficulties.
Goren/Maaleh Yosef: Many residents lack individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); shelters not in optimal condition; some residents have distant shelters.
Goren/Maaleh Yosef: Increase in calls to emergency hotline 106.
Goren/Maaleh Yosef: Elderly population in distress—difficulty reaching safe rooms; some injured.
Goren/Maaleh Yosef: Need for military presence (soldier-teachers/מורות חיילות) for public messaging and guidance.
Abdon/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Residents not leaving; additional armored field booths (מיגוניות) provided.
Abdon: HFC community coordinator recruiting volunteers; women's evening and adult activities organized; informal activity ongoing.
Abdon: Not all elderly have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters distant; residents unable to reach shelters in time.
Abdon: Distrust of military—'The army does not tell the truth.'
Liman: Central distress—lack of activities for children.
Liman: Difficulty protecting farmers' security; known protection gaps in process of being addressed.
Liman: HFC volunteer corps functioning well overall; request for soldier-teachers (מורות חיילות).
Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Sense of fatigue and erosion (שחיקה) from ongoing situation.

Granot HaGalil: Community resilience expressed as willingness to enable what is possible without distraction; most population returned; young functioning population; coping discourse; basic youth activity; readiness unit (כיתת כוננות) exists; community communication without toxic discourse; good relationship with council and Home Front Command.

Granot HaGalil: Protection gaps; elderly lack protection; HFC volunteer corps not fully operational; no designated person/body responsible for mapping elderly and people with disabilities; welfare services not connected to this population; gap in education staff.

Granot HaGalil: Elderly and those with special needs lack 'parent figures'—no community body ensuring comprehensive care; isolated populations including long-time residents, urban residents, families with special-needs children, and women whose families are in military service.

Aven Menahem/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Residents expressed: 'We are mentally ill people living here.' Sense of abandonment: 'We are the periphery of the periphery.' Painful to see families and children. Deep distrust of authorities.
Aven Menahem: Significant disruption to daily life routines; no spaces for social activity under protection; tourism inactive; agriculture significantly damaged.
Aven Menahem: Serious problem with individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters in poor maintenance condition; HFC volunteer corps not fully operational; limited number of volunteers.
Aven Menahem: Community involvement and mutual aid when needed.

Aven Menahem: Evidence of children struggling with difficulty; families without family support network; deep erosion and difficulty; urgent need for short-term resilience strengthening alongside long-term solutions.
Matta/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Community cohesion significantly strengthened; overall sense of security; extensive protection in public space.
Matta: Families without individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); need for sewage infrastructure repair.
Matta: Community coordinator working at full capacity; need for decompression activities for children and families.
Batzet/Matte Asher (Bareqem): Community managing with strong leadership and cooperation among role-holders.
Batzet: Beginning to enter emergency routine; farmers working and people going to work; cyclical work due to lack of suitable shelters.

Batzet: Children and youth at home using Zoom with limited success; difficulty implementing education frameworks; workers not arriving; difficulty with youth; substance use and alcohol complications discovered.

Batzet: HFC volunteer corps active; volunteers; soldier-teachers; army education core (גרעין נח"ל); light shelter renovation for educational activity; assistance with transportation for army education core to function.

Psuta (Bareqem): Overall resilience present but political instability affecting it; people in emergency routine but more free; workshops and learning centers for essential workers and medical staff; decompression workshops and learning center for high school students; student council activity.

Psuta: One shelter unsuitable for use; weak volunteer network; not all arriving; only one trained; clubs for elderly and special needs closed and difficult to visit; experiencing loneliness and difficulty; welfare department struggling to reach all residents for visits.
Psuta: Extensive informal activities through education department.

Alkosh/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Population obedient to policy and HFC directives; elderly struggling to reach protected areas; general apathy expressed in lack of volunteering for leisure activities and community life; no community cohesion; no inspiring leadership for action.
Alkosh: HFC volunteer corps includes only the coordinator, no additional functionaries; limited enrichment activity for children; need for siren repair and other security gaps.
Horfish/Matte Asher (Bareqem): Authority broadcasting resilience and high control in settlement; strong settlement.
Horfish: Full emergency routine; private businesses opening; council-related matters showing policy hardening.
Horfish: No activity even in public shelters; frameworks not working for elderly, women, and special populations—all cancelled, some minimal via Zoom.
Horfish: Loneliness; frameworks not working for elderly, women, and special populations.

Kibbutz Ayalon/Matte Asher (Bareqem): Evacuation created dependency among some residents for basic needs (cleaning, repairs, food, etc.); residents still struggling to return to autonomous functioning; sense of broken community cohesion following evacuation in Iron Swords War; residents more autonomous and less engaged in community activities.

Kibbutz Ayalon: Shelter quality low—old systems, stuffy; no protection in local clinic—need to restore medical/clinic response; many essential workers with uncertainty due to lack of answers and no solutions for their children.
Kibbutz Ayalon: Informal education—activity exists but relatively limited because instructors partly not kibbutz residents and did not return.

Yaara/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Silence in streets, almost no vehicles; no open businesses; those remaining are confined, going out only if necessary; no frameworks; informal education for some kindergarten-early elementary children.
Yaara: Those without individual safe rooms (ממ"ד) evacuated autonomously; those with shelters take shelter.

Yaara: Public shelters serve worshippers and informal frameworks but too small to contain activity, or defense policy does not allow (over 50 people); HFC volunteer corps attempting population survey but only 5 out of over 250 families.
Yaara: Loneliness, fatalistic because no one will help evacuate them to safe room when needed (moving slowly).
Manot/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Not many people on streets but less tension, less depressing to be there; those spoken with were in elevated mood.
Manot: No frameworks and desire for informal education or opening frameworks for kindergarten-elementary in settlement areas; not working except remotely; many mobilized to reserves.
Manot: HFC volunteer corps and organizations bringing supplies and services via WhatsApp; care for each other within family framework.
Manot: Residents caring for each other within family framework; apparently sent aid packages; less fear of approaching nearby communities to help compared to settlements closer to fence.
Netu'a/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Residents not wanting evacuation except parents with children (children reluctant); established residents wanting to stay in homes.
Netu'a: Families in homes trying to live under emergency routine; HFC in contact with residents providing response to vulnerable populations.

Netu'a: Residents have resilience as long as IDF does its job; settlement in process of coping and growth in community processes even before war; after return from evacuation, positive community recovery and rehabilitation evident; resilience components present—formal and informal leadership performing trust-building processes with community; internal forces and HFC and readiness unit and rabbi working in good communication.
Shtula/Maaleh Yosef (Bareqem): Families from religious core left; weakening of community resilience.
Shtula: Nervousness about crisis; burnout (שחיקה) of role-holders; resilience not high but internal forces holding settlement; volunteers from outside coming to help.
Shtula: Elderly—inability to leave home; need for medication and food supplies; informal education—limited activity with desire to increase responses.
Shtula: HFC team contacting all vulnerable populations with emphasis on widows and elderly; help bringing medicines and food through coordinated purchases among residents or volunteers.
Arraba al-Aramsha/Matte Asher (Bareqem): No resident movement; rumor about evacuation in Iron Swords War; shelters not providing sufficient response; no children's activities during Ramadan.
Arraba al-Aramsha: Residents filming during alerts.

Adamit/Matte Asher (Bareqem): Most residents in settlement; readiness unit needing refresher; HFC functioning toward elderly and special needs; parents with small children without protection; parents exhausted but not using resilience services.
Adamit: Youth mobilized to help in kibbutz; caring for people staying in shelters.
Kibbutz Snir/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Narrative of resilience; high mutual aid; informal activity especially afternoons in shelters; WhatsApp group use.

Kibbutz Snir: Lack of armored field booth (מיגונית) in expansion neighborhood; no siren coverage; need for soldier-teachers and teachers; elderly—difficulty reaching shelters due to zero alert time and doctor rarely arriving.
Kibbutz Snir: Problem—shared military and civilian command structure; needs separation.

Beit Hillel/Mevuot Hermon (Hiram): Expansion residents more hysterical (former Kiryat Shmona residents); no intention to leave; students present who do not want to leave; decompression activity—1-1.5 hours; work continuity variable; functional continuity 60%; no extensive activity for elderly; protection gaps in elderly club; youth club without standard protection; children's shelter—infrastructure issue; individual safe room (ממ"ד) situation improved significantly; shopping trips to Kiryat Shmona; HFC—no chair; limited volunteer network but operating by sub-teams; decompression activity for elderly; decompression for youth and children.
Beit Hillel: Two psychologists on site; resilience present.
Dafna/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Population coping; informal network operating; no protection gaps.
Dafna: Emergency and resilience team established—urgent need for HFC commander.
Dafna: Elderly—loneliness issue.
Meiyim Baruch/Galil Elyon (Hiram): No desire to evacuate; strong community and strong authority.

Meiyim Baruch: Lack of armored field booths (מיגוניות) at bus station and two at playgrounds; elderly and welfare population being treated; people with disabilities receiving response; lack of standard protection in informal education network.
Kibbutz Dan/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Strong community coping; use of community resources including HFC; response to population with disabilities and elderly; informal activity occurring.
Kibbutz Dan: No protection in community buildings; need for soldier-teachers; need for siren addition check.

Meshgav Am/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Most not ready to leave; took in six new families; doing children's activities; request for two soldier-teachers; functional continuity; HFC—four residents; community action present; optimal response to elderly; residents with mental health trauma from war and evacuation; not all understand this will be long.
Meshgav Am: Residents with psychological trauma from war and evacuation; people tired and not sleeping well at night.
Meshgav Am: Lack of firefighters and emergency response team; request for decompression; soldier-teachers as much as possible; protection priority.
Manara/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Strong community; decompression activity starting tomorrow; strong HFC; volunteers; preparatory program.

Manara: Significant protection gaps; missing welfare department—not staffed; elderly—no meetings due to lack of public space; difficulty descending stairs; age-based division; need for soldier-teachers to prevent burnout of education volunteers; support for decompression; need for decompression outings.

Tzavon: Many decompression activities for children and youth; emphasis on community cohesion and not evacuating; HFC working well; volunteers hosting decompression workshops; amazing initiatives in community resilience context.

Tzavon: Agriculture—missing armored field booth (מיגונית); old neighborhood—no individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); only one shelter for entire neighborhood; false alerts lowering resilience; need for protection reinforcement.
Karem Ben Zimra: No community activity; decompression activity for youth—two hours daily; bureaucracy of government ministries.
Kfar Giladi/Galil Elyon (Hiram): Narrative of strong community against state neglect and denial of border settlement status.
Kfar Giladi: Decompression for elderly within protected space; volunteer network for elderly; community action present.

Kfar Giladi: Inability to provide response for ages 0-6; significant protection gaps; shelters do not contain all residents without protection; challenge with bedridden patients unable to take shelter; increase in calls to community resilience team; youth wandering; worsening of mental health condition; need for messaging that IDF is with us.
Mevuot Hermon - Shar Yishuv (Hiram): Student departure.

Mevuot Hermon - Shar Yishuv: Rest in positive spirit; resilience discourse; resources and volunteer network present—not always the right people; activity for children; residents feeling flooded with military personnel without coverage.
Mevuot Hermon - Shar Yishuv: Protection gaps; elderly—shelter gaps, unable to always reach protected space; need for ventilation especially for elderly.
Ramot Naftali/Mevuot Hermon (Hiram): Residents okay; surprise that enemy not defeated; less visible in current round; reduced functional continuity—low-dose activity.

Ramot Naftali: Central challenge—elderly protection; elderly struggling to reach shelter during defense; generator shortage for settlement center; lack of refresher program for elderly and families with small children; readiness unit not trained on 'Noah's Ark' protocol.

Margelit/Mevuot Hermon (Hiram): Aging population rooted in land; resilience discourse; council enveloping; many protection gaps; less mutual responsibility; elderly needing ventilation; moving to protected housing seen as problematic; residents feeling like targets; without sense of security, in 10-20 years no residents; barely managing to open kindergarten due to lack of children.
Yir'on: Very active HFC—received donation; concern for elderly in community; informal activity for children and youth; employment—tourism business affected; expectation for continued visits.
